name: How do I know if my old garage is worth converting?

mainEntity.name: What signs mean a garage conversion will be straightforward versus a money pit?
mainEntity.text: What signs mean a garage conversion will be straightforward versus a money pit?

acceptedAnswer.text: An old garage is a good conversion candidate when the shell is sound and the layout already fits a livable floor plan. The biggest red flags are structural settlement, low ceilings, moisture damage, undocumented alterations, and obvious code issues. If the slab is cracked badly or the framing is deteriorated, costs can rise quickly enough that a new detached build becomes more attractive. Homeowners should also verify whether the garage was built with permits and whether the footprint works for a bedroom, bath, and kitchen without awkward compromises. A worthwhile conversion is one where the existing structure saves enough time and money to justify the work needed to make it truly habitable. If the garage is heavily compromised, starting fresh may provide better value and fewer surprises.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage is usually worth converting when the slab, framing, roof, and footprint are in decent condition and the structure can be upgraded without major structural corrections. Severe settling, low ceiling height, or poor permit history can make the project expensive.
